Your local logging setup.

Application release v0.1 · 10 October 2026. The receiver and dashboard are implemented; ESP32 capture firmware and bike-specific CAN definitions are pending.

1. Run the receiver

With Python 3.11 or later, open a terminal in the Bee Link app folder:

python server.py

On the development Windows machine, start-local.ps1 also locates the bundled Python runtime. Open http://127.0.0.1:8765, then choose Connection & setup → Connect. The empty receiver correctly shows missing signals.

2. Capture on the bike

The intended gateway is an ESP32, protected listen-only CAN interface, GPS and microSD. It must log to SD before trying Wi-Fi, preserve acquisition timestamps and keep immutable capture/sequence identities. Firmware, actual pins, bitrate and electrical validation are still required. Sleeping vehicle electronics may emit no readings.

3. Connect over home Wi-Fi

Set BEELINK_TOKEN to a random secret of at least 24 characters, then start the receiver with --host 0.0.0.0. Open its LAN address from your phone and enter the token in Connection & setup. The token stays in that tab’s memory. This server is intended for a trusted home network; use a trusted HTTPS proxy for shared/untrusted access.

The full README contains Windows and Docker examples. No router or firewall settings are changed by this app.

4. Upload captures

Future firmware sends batches to POST /api/ingest. A JSON body has a samples array. Each sample needs schema_version 1, device_id, capture_id, sequence, UTC capture timestamp, source (can / gnss / mixed), variant, decoder_version, signals and frames. Raw frames alone are accepted.

python tools/upload_capture.py capture.jsonl

That tool uploads an SD export from a PC/Pi. It never alters the original file and waits for acknowledged sequence identities. Re-running identical captures is safe. Browser imports replay locally and do not add to the real database.

5. Add Home Assistant sensors

Configure Home Assistant MQTT and your private Mosquitto broker. Install and run the optional bridge beside the receiver:

python -m pip install -r requirements-mqtt.txt
python mqtt_bridge.py --broker YOUR_BROKER_LAN_IP

Provide MQTT_USERNAME, MQTT_PASSWORD and BEELINK_TOKEN through the environment as applicable. Only fresh verified readings are published by default. --include-provisional is an explicit development option. --gps opts in to publishing location to your broker. --tls --port 8883 supports a broker configured with trusted TLS.

Discovery and process availability are retained; sensor state is not. Sensors expire after 15 seconds without updates. Old ride uploads remain in SQLite and do not become retroactive Home Assistant history.

6. Preserve the log

SQLite is stored in data/bee-link.sqlite. There is no automatic purge. Monitor free space and keep original SD captures. Use JSONL export for portable raw/decoded captures. CSV contains decoded readings only.

Back up through SQLite's online backup API, or stop the server before copying its database. Copying only the main file while WAL writes are running can miss data. Home Assistant's default short-term recorder retention is ten days; configure it deliberately.

Supported signal units

Charge (%), pack voltage (V), current (A), speed (km/h), explicit temperatures (°C), odometer (km), cell_NN_v group voltages, GPS latitude/longitude (degrees), actual GPS accuracy (m) and satellite count. The producer must document current sign. HDOP must not be labelled as metre accuracy.

Values need confidence and evidence. Every live signal keeps its own timestamp and turns missing/stale after ten seconds without a fresh capture. No signal layout is verified for the bike yet.
